\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} Annual panel 1996--2023, no microstates. Local projections of 100 $\times$ log GDP per capita from t $-$ 1 to t + h on a wage bill shock (percentage points of GDP), with two lags of the shock and of growth and country and year fixed effects; h = $-$1 is zero by construction. Shocks: (a) 100 $\times$ (W\_{t$-$1}/P\_{t$-$2} $-$ W\_{t$-$2}/P\_{t$-$2}) / y\_{t$-$2}, dated in t $-$ 1 and deflated by the deflator of t $-$ 2, so it uses no current prices or output; (b) residual of the current shock (100 $\times$ (W\_t/P\_t $-$ W\_{t$-$1}/P\_{t$-$1}) / y\_{t$-$1}) on current growth and two lags, with country-specific slopes and country and year fixed effects; (c) the current shock deflated by the deflator of t $-$ 1. Inference: Driscoll-Kraay standard errors (maximum lag 3); lag-augmented local projections (Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Møller, 2021: one more lag of the shock and of growth, heteroskedasticity-robust errors); half-panel jackknife bias correction (2 $\times$ full sample $-$ mean of 1996--2009 and 2010--2023), with the full-sample Driscoll-Kraay standard error. Shock (b) is a generated regressor: its standard errors and 95\% CIs come from a country block bootstrap that re-estimates the purging regression in each of 999 replications (percentile CI in the first column; lag-augmented column with robust errors that ignore the generated-regressor step). Panel B: shock (a) interacted with merit above the median in t $-$ 2 (V-Dem), with the total shock as control, so the coefficient is high $-$ low; Romano--Wolf step-down p over h = 0--6, 999 country draws. Stars from the standard errors of each column; 95\% CIs in brackets. Exploratory (pre-registered in the plan addendum). * p<0.10, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01.\end{minipage}
